task.title: Cut patch releases to an older line without releasing main
task.description:
Every release is cut from main today, and main already carries the next minor by the time a fix to the last stable release is wanted, so there is no way to ship, say, v0.5.2 once v0.6.0 work has landed. Decide how patch releases to an older line are cut and make the release path support it.

Known constraints from the current release path:
- cut-release.yml and release-pr.yml refuse any branch other than main; only a hand-pushed tag bypasses them, and nothing then checks the tag sits on a supported line. Allow release/X.Y branches (or an equivalent) in both triggers, and validate that a tag is on a supported branch.
- A backport tag cascades into the desktop release. plan-desktop-release.sh refuses a desktop tag that does not clear the newest desktop tag, and if it did not, publish-desktop-release.sh would move desktop-latest (the site download links and the updater address) backward. The rolling release and the Homebrew tap must only be refreshed when the release being published is newer than what they currently serve.
- check-release-changelog.sh reads the topmost ## vX.Y.Z heading and the Unreleased section as next-minor material; a backport entry needs a rule for where it is written and how it is forward-ported to main.
- Keep the trunk. Release branches should be created on demand from the tag being patched, not maintained continuously.

Build this the first time a user on an older release needs a fix without taking the next minor; until then, fixes ship in the next release from main.
